[Discussion]If Downwell had been released in 1995, how would have people thought about this game back then and now?

I think it probably would have done pretty well, but the art for it would have been way more awesome. It would probably be the manliest dude with the coolest rocket boots you've ever seen instead of the cutesy bubble guy the cover art is now. At least in America, it would be.

I haven't played it, but I think a lot of people would have HATED the current generation of roguelikes and retro games. They had not lived through a decade worth of games where you can't fail, so to them the notion of a game that glorifies death and failure, and in fact encourages those things to frequently happen instead of just having a reasonable difficulty level would make no sense at all.

Ninja Gaiden was released in 1988, and by 1991, every variation on the Famicom/NES had a version of it. Gamers were pretty accustomed to games where you die constantly. Actually, most games were still being made with challenge in mind. We hadn't come down off the arcade high quite yet, and weren't fully accustomed to thinking of game design for home play.

You died often in old games, but they were hard to draw out limited content, not because getting killed a bunch was their way of being a counter-development to games where you practically can't fail. Personally at least I can tell the difference when I play old games vs. newer retro games in how that difference feels to the player.
And if was made back then, it would probably just be hard, and not have failure built in as a mechanic.
